name: seg7
author: ULX3S Digital Design Course
description: Lesson 02 - a 7-segment hex decoder: 4 bits in, 7 segments out.
info:
## Lesson 02 - the hex decoder

Set the four slide switches to a hex digit and read the segment pattern on `led[6:0]`, in the order `abcdefg`:

```
     aaaa        led_6 = a   top
    f    b       led_5 = b   top right
    f    b       led_4 = c   bottom right
     gggg        led_3 = d   bottom
    e    c       led_2 = e   bottom left
    e    c       led_1 = f   top left
     dddd        led_0 = g   middle
```

Switches at `1010` (hex A) should give `1110111`.

### The thing to notice

The code block holds a 16-way `case`. The lesson's `seg7_rom` module expresses the identical truth table as an array of constants instead - and both cost exactly **7 LUT4**. A `case` is not 'logic' and an array is not 'memory'; both describe a function of four inputs, and only the function survives.

### Why this block and not the whole lesson

An Icestudio code block cannot instantiate other modules, so the lesson's `comb_top` (which wires seg7, an adder and a mux together) cannot be generated as one block. Composing modules is what the Icestudio canvas itself is for - that is the next step, and lesson 03 starts putting reusable blocks in `icestudio/collections/`.
